name: Audionotes
summary: AI note-taker that turns voice recordings, audio and video files, YouTube links and text into transcripts, summaries and custom notes you can chat with, on iOS, Android, web and Mac.
best_for: individual professionals, students and journalers who want voice memos, recordings, files and YouTube videos turned into transcripts, summaries and notes they can chat with, on phone, web and Mac
skip_if: you need team administration below five users or want to pay monthly without committing to a year; or you mainly need to record calls played through your speakers
honest_knock: Free voice notes stop at one minute each, so it is a trial for anything longer than a quick thought. The support page says paid subscriptions are not refunded. The app records from the device microphone, not from the speakers, and the terms mention Personal and Ultra plans that the pricing page does not show.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-10-15 on audionotes.app/pricing, the terms at audionotes.app/tos and the refund policy; the page shows $ without naming a currency) Three plans on the pricing page. Free is $0 forever with no credit card: unlimited voice notes of up to 1 minute each and unlimited text notes of up to 20,000 characters. Pro is $129.99 a year and lists chat with your notes, custom prompts and Notion, Zapier and webhook integrations. On Pro a recording can run up to 6 hours, a file upload up to 500 MB, a YouTube video up to 6 hours, a text note up to 20,000 characters and an image up to 20 MB. Enterprise is custom, for teams of 5 or more. The terms add a daily allowance: Personal and Pro accounts may process up to 600 minutes of media transcription a day. The terms and refund policy also mention Personal and Ultra plans that are not on the pricing page. The support page says Audionotes does not refund paid subscriptions, while the refund policy allows cancelling at any time, keeps access until the end of the paid period, and lists legal exceptions and case-by-case refunds.

schema_offer.description: Pro, billed yearly; recordings up to 6 hours and file uploads up to 500 MB; the terms allow up to 600 minutes of transcription a day on Personal and Pro; Free $0 with voice notes capped at 1 minute each; Enterprise custom for teams of 5+; the page shows $ without a currency code. Read on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-10-15.

compare_with.name: WhisperTranscribe
compare_with.why: WhisperTranscribe is in our dossiers too and is the closer pick for longer recordings: its Starter plan was $19.99 a month billed yearly for 320 minutes when we read it on 14 October 2026, aimed at podcasters, researchers and small teams. Audionotes is a personal note-taker with a free tier of unlimited one-minute voice notes and Pro at $129.99 a year. For daily voice notes and summaries, Audionotes; for transcribing long audio by the hour, WhisperTranscribe.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 30 October 2026 on the Free plan: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We wrote two made-up text notes with a tag and looked for ways to get them out again.
findings: The Free plan has 'Limited features and 1 min per recording'. No card was asked and there is no trial end date.
Text notes save automatically and keep accents and quotes exactly.
We found no export: the note menu only offers tag, move and delete, and the settings have no data export.

The only way to take a note out is 'Copy Transcript', which copies to your clipboard. The title and tags are not included, a blank line is added between paragraphs, and 'via Audionotes.app' is added at the end.
Notes can also go out through Notion, WhatsApp, Zapier and webhooks, but each needs a connection we did not make.
